ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In $\triangle ACB$, $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, $AB=4$, and $BC=3$. Squares are constructed externally on each of the three sides. Connecting the vertices of these squares forms a hexagon DEFGHI. What is the area of hexagon DEFGHI?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, \\
in $\triangle ABC$, since $AB=4$ and $BC=3$, \\
therefore $AC=\sqrt{AB^{2}+BC^{2}}=\sqrt{4^{2}+3^{2}}=5$. \\
Since quadrilaterals ABDE, BCGF, and ACHM are all squares, \\
therefore $\angle ABD=\angle CBF=\angle BAE=\angle CAM=\angle ACH=\angle GCH=90^\circ$, BD=BA, AM=AC, CBN=CG, $S_{\text{square ABDE}}=4^{2}=16$, $S_{\text{square ACHM}}=5^{2}=25$, $S_{\text{square BCGF}}=3^{2}=9$, \\
therefore, $\angle DBF+\angle ABC=180^\circ$, $\angle MAE+\angle BAC=180^\circ$, $\angle ACB+\angle HCG=180^\circ$, \\
draw IM$\perp$DA to intersect the extension line of DA at M, \\
therefore $\angle M=\angle ABC=90^\circ$, \\
since $\angle DAI+\angle MAI=\angle DAI+\angle BAC=180^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle IAM=\angle BAC$, \\
in $\triangle AMI$ and $\triangle BAC$, \\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}\angle M=\angle ABC \\ \angle BAC=\angle MAI \\ AC=AI \end{array}\right.$ \\
therefore $\triangle AMI \cong \triangle ABC$, \\
hence AB=AM, \\
thus AD=AM, \\
thus $S_{\triangle AMI}=S_{\triangle ABC}=S_{\triangle ADI}$, \\
Similarly, $S_{\triangle BEF}=S_{\triangle ABC}$, $S_{\triangle CHG}=S_{\triangle ABC}$, \\
thus $S_{\triangle DBF}=S_{\triangle MAE}=S_{\triangle HCG}=S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times 4=6$, \\
therefore the area of the hexagon DEMHGF=$25+16+9+4\times6=\boxed{74}$.

raw_record.original_question: In $\triangle ACB$, $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, $AB=4$, and $BC=3$. Squares are constructed externally on each of the three sides. Connecting the vertices of these squares forms a hexagon DEFGHI. What is the area of hexagon DEFGHI?
raw_record.answer: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, since $AB=4$ and $BC=3$, therefore $AC=\sqrt{AB^{2}+BC^{2}}=\sqrt{4^{2}+3^{2}}=5$. Since quadrilaterals ABDE, BCGF, and ACHM are all squares, therefore $\angle ABD=\angle CBF=\angle BAE=\angle CAM=\angle ACH=\angle GCH=90^\circ$, $BD=BA$, $AM=AC$, $CBN=CG$, $S_{\text{square ABDE}}=4^{2}=16$, $S_{\text{square ACHM}}=5^{2}=25$, $S_{\text{square BCGF}}=3^{2}=9$. Therefore, $\angle DBF+\angle ABC=180^\circ$, $\angle MAE+\angle BAC=180^\circ$, $\angle ACB+\angle HCG=180^\circ$. Draw $IM\perp DA$ to intersect the extension line of $DA$ at $M$, therefore $\angle M=\angle ABC=90^\circ$. Since $\angle DAI+\angle MAI=\angle DAI+\angle BAC=180^\circ$, therefore $\angle IAM=\angle BAC$. In $\triangle AMI$ and $\triangle BAC$, $\angle M=\angle ABC$, $\angle BAC=\angle MAI$, and $AC=AI$, therefore $\triangle AMI \cong \triangle BAC$, hence $AB=AM$, thus $AD=AM$, thus $S_{\triangle AMI}=S_{\triangle ABC}=S_{\triangle ADI}$. Similarly, $S_{\triangle BEF}=S_{\triangle ABC}$, $S_{\triangle CHG}=S_{\triangle ABC}$, thus $S_{\triangle DBF}=S_{\triangle MAE}=S_{\triangle HCG}=S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times 4=6$. Therefore the area of the hexagon $DEMHGF=25+16+9+4\times 6=\boxed{74}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description first: The attached diagram shows a central right triangle ACB, with A above B and C to the right of B; the right angle is at B. A square ABDE is drawn externally to the left of side AB, a square BCGF is drawn externally below side BC, and a square ACIH is drawn externally on side AC. The outer vertices D, E, F, G, H, I are connected to form the hexagon DEFGHI. Reasoning: Since AB=4, BC=3, and ∠ABC=90°, the hypotenuse is AC=sqrt(4^2+3^2)=5. Drawing AB, BC, and AC partitions the hexagon into the three squares, the central triangle ABC, and the three corner triangles EBF, GCH, and IAD. The square areas are 4^2=16, 3^2=9, and 5^2=25. The central triangle area is (1/2)*4*3=6. For the corner triangles: EBF has side lengths EB=4 and BF=3 with included right angle, so its area is 6. Also, because square sides are perpendicular to the corresponding triangle sides, ∠GCH is supplementary to ∠ACB and ∠IAD is supplementary to ∠BAC, so using sin(180°-θ)=sin θ, each of GCH and IAD has the same area as triangle ABC, namely 6. Therefore the hexagon area is 16+9+25+6+3*6=74.
